paragraphs.source_en: Tonight, we are stranded outside Dagu Strait, exiles upon a sea with no shore, and we speak our sorrow to grief itself. A single lantern on the mast sways against the wind: the sky is dim, veiled in layered cloud, and that flashing light is a sea-fire probing the dark. You said that what we call not-free is the unrest of these times. But even this turmoil will come to an end, who then has the right to say that life is free? Hope for today becomes, by tomorrow, a dull sorrow. Starlight looks down coldly from beyond the sky, and life is only a clinging foam within the breakers. I now pace the bleak, cold deck, hearing the sea-foam rise and fall and burst, my heart as empty as an unbroken tide. Only a shred of cloud-shadow sways in the heart of this lake— one inexplicable, tangled dream, one dream one cannot bear to decipher. Written on March 12, 1926.

paragraphs.source_zh:
今夜困守在大沽口外：

絕海裏的俘虜，

對著憂愁申訴；

桅上的孤燈在風前搖擺：

天昏昏有層雲裏，

那掣電是探海火！

你說不自由是這變亂的時光？

但變亂還有時罷休，

誰敢說人生有自由？

今天的希望變作明天的悵惘；

星光在天外冷眼瞅，

人生是浪花裏的浮漚！

我此時在凄冷的甲板上徘徊，

聽海濤遲遲的吐沫，

心空如不波的潮水；

只一絲雲影在這湖心裏晃動──

不曾參透的一個迷夢，

不忍參透的一個迷夢！

一九二六年三月十二日作
